set.explanation: Crescendo rest angina with normal ECG and troponin is unstable angina: admit and add anticoagulation (LMWH/fondaparinux). Thrombolysis is only for ST elevation.

why: Earliest-source rule: PreTest version kept instead of Other Sources
Same idea as cad-0116 (unstable angina: add LMWH); earlier source kept

set.stem: During the Valsalva manoeuvre in a patient with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, what happens to the intensity of the murmur?
set.explanation: Valsalva (like standing) reduces preload, the LV cavity shrinks and outflow obstruction worsens, so the HCM murmur gets louder; squatting and handgrip soften it.

why: Earliest-source rule: Log Book version kept instead of Harrison
Same idea as hf-0035 (HCM murmur louder with Valsalva/standing)

set.explanation: Pulseless VF is a shockable rhythm: defibrillate immediately, then 2 min CPR. Adrenaline is given after the third shock; bicarbonate and calcium are not routine.

why: Earliest-source rule (Crash Course kept over PreTest); bicarbonate unit fixed (mmol) and shock energy updated to biphasic
Same idea as arr-0070 (shockable arrest: immediate defibrillation)

set.explanation: Irregular tachycardia without P waves is AF; in a stable patient first-line rate control is a beta-blocker (bisoprolol) or rate-limiting CCB. Flecainide is for rhythm control in structurally normal hearts.

why: Earliest-source rule (Crash Course kept over Passmedicine); lignocaine renamed lidocaine
Same idea as arr-0074 (AF rate control with bisoprolol)

set.stem: A 42-year-old woman presents with breathlessness and chest discomfort. There is a loud first heart sound, an opening snap after S2 and a low-pitched mid-diastolic murmur at the apex. Which valve lesion is most likely?
set.explanation: Loud S1, opening snap and an apical mid-diastolic rumble are mitral stenosis, usually rheumatic. Tricuspid stenosis is at the lower left sternal edge; aortic stenosis is systolic.

why: Earliest-source rule (Formative kept over Crash Course); murmur site corrected to the apex
Same idea as valv-0011 (mitral stenosis signs)

set.stem: A 65-year-old man has 3 months of exertional central chest pain and breathlessness that settle with rest, and lately dizziness on exertion. There is an ejection systolic murmur radiating to the carotids. ECG shows tall R waves in I, aVL and V4–V6 with deep S waves in V1–V3. What is the most likely diagnosis?
set.explanation: Exertional angina, dyspnoea and dizziness/syncope with an ejection murmur and LVH on ECG is severe aortic stenosis. HCM is younger, and its murmur does not radiate to the carotids.

why: Earliest-source rule (Crash Course kept over PreTest); garbled ECG description corrected to LVH
Same idea as valv-0030 (classic triad of aortic stenosis)

set.stem: A 43-year-old woman with known breast cancer has increasing breathlessness. Heart sounds are soft and the apex beat cannot be felt. Which investigation is most likely to make the diagnosis?
set.explanation: Soft heart sounds and an impalpable apex in a patient with cancer suggest a malignant pericardial effusion; echocardiography confirms it and shows tamponade physiology.

why: Earliest-source rule (Crash Course kept over PreTest); stem tidied
Same idea as peri-0039 (suspected pericardial effusion: echocardiography)
Repointed to the new survivor peri-0039

set.stem: A 63-year-old man with hypertension presents to the emergency department with sudden-onset tearing chest pain radiating to the back. What is the most likely diagnosis?
set.explanation: Sudden tearing pain radiating to the back in a hypertensive patient is aortic dissection until proved otherwise; confirm with CT aortography and control BP and heart rate.

why: Earliest-source rule (Previous CVS kept over Log Book)
Same idea as cad-0131 (aortic dissection)

set.explanation: COPD is obstructive: post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC < 0.70, with gas trapping (raised RV/TLC) and low DLCO in emphysema. A low TLC means restriction.

why: Earliest-source rule (Log Book kept over Harrison)
Same idea as airway-0057 (PFTs in COPD)

set.stem: Which of the following is least useful in assessing the prognosis of community-acquired pneumonia?
set.explanation: CURB-65 uses confusion, urea > 7 mmol/L, RR ≥ 30, low BP and age ≥ 65; CRP is useful for diagnosis and monitoring but is not a severity criterion.

why: Earliest-source rule (Previous Respiratory kept over PasTest); units clarified
Same idea as resinf-0051 (CURB-65 prognostic factors)

set.stem: A 48-year-old man has symptomatic obstructive sleep apnoea with an apnoea–hypopnoea index of 42/hour. What is the most appropriate initial therapy?
set.explanation: AHI ≥ 30/h is severe OSA: CPAP is first line and improves sleepiness and BP. Oral devices suit mild disease; weight loss helps but is not enough alone.

why: Earliest-source rule (Harrison kept over Crash Course)
Same idea as resx-0044 (OSA: CPAP)
